description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis, labeled Initial Confidence, has a linear scale, ranging from 0.91 to 0.99 with a tick label interval of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled Accuracy, also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 0.8 with a tick label interval of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy, represented by a solid blue line with circle markers, starts at approximately 0.89 at an Initial Confidence of 0.91 and remains relatively stable, with a slight peak at 0.93, before decreasing to around 0.86 at 0.99; Δ Accuracy, depicted by a dashed orange line with diamond markers, begins at about 0.55 at 0.91, peaks at 0.65 at 0.92, and then declines to around 0.15 at 0.99; Initial Accuracy, shown as a dash-dotted green line with square markers, starts at approximately 0.27 at 0.91, decreases to 0.25 at 0.92, and then generally increases to around 0.81 at 0.985 before decreasing to 0.75 at 0.99.
